newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie on the slide as CRB hits two-yr low.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie on the slide as CRB hits two-yr low.

text.p: *AUD makes new 18-month low at $0.7420 as CRB index plunges to a two-year trough and endless rate cut talk saps sentiment
*Gold sales led index lower but other commodities also soft and major trend downturns threaten for both CRB and A$
*Break of $0.7440 has opened way to $0.7390 and eventually 73 cents, while $0.7470 needed to pause and $0.7570 to reverse
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the local dollar had eked out a bounce to US$0.7443/48 to be steady on Monday's weak close having skidded from US$0.7520 late here Friday.

Further support levels were seen at US$0.7390 and US$0.7350 but analysts thought last year's low of 73 cents would act as a strong attractor now. A rally past US$0.7470 would signal a pause, while US$0.7570 would have to be cleared to counter the immediate bearish trend.
Without that, analysts saw a real risk the long bull run the A$ has enjoyed since troughing at 64 cents in late 1993 might be coming to an end to be replaced by a new bear phase.
Most had been assuming the five cent of losses suffered since March was just a correction in the uptrend, exacerbated by the surprise easing in official interest rates on May 23.
Talk of yet another cut took money rates below those in the U.S. for the first time since domestic markets were deregulated in 1983 and a lot of short term money moved deserted the A$.

But still most analysts had thought strengthening world growth would lead to rising commodity prices later in the year which in turn would support the dollar. The growth was indeed coming but commodity prices were not responding as planned, with the CRB index down 21 points or eight percent since mid-May.
The latest dive in the CRB, which is closely followed by U.S. investors, was important since it was broad-based and confirmed a breach of major chart support at 236.00.

It took the index out of a rising channel which has lasted since early 1993 when it was languishing at 198.00 and left the index within spitting distance of the 231.00 level, which would mark a 50 percent retracement of the entire rally to a 257.00 peak in April last year.
Analysts noted a full 61.8 percent retracement would take it back to 223.00 and the dollar toward 70 cents.
